observations:
Torah #252 is one of the shortest teachings in Likutay Moharan — two sentences, aphoristic in form. A new package requires three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain. This Torah contains no bechina language whatsoever. The full text reads:

כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ אַחְדוּת בֵּין הַצַּדִּיקִים, אֵין הַצְּדָקָה מַזֶּקֶת... וְכֵן עַל־יְדֵי זֶה יְכוֹלִים שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְהָאָדָם מְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ בֶּאֱמֶת, וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא יַזִּיק לוֹ, וְיִשָּׁאֵר בַּחַיִּים.

The structure is purely eitza: unity among tzaddikim enables extraordinary outcomes (charity without loss; self-sacrifice without death). Neither 'צדקה' nor 'מסירת נפש' is described as a 'בְּחִינַת' of anything else. The two outcomes — giving without losing and dying without dying — are presented as parallel results of the same cause (unity), but they are not declared equivalent to each other through bechina language; they are parallel eitzas from a single source. Even if one were to speculatively group צדקה and מסירת נפש as two faces of the same concept (total giving of self), the text does not make this equation explicit, and doing so would project bechina structure onto an eitza-only text. The correct representation of this Torah in the map is as a pure eitza chain: [אחדות הצדיקים] →eitza→ [צדקה ללא חסרון] + [מסירת נפש ללא מיתה].
